brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall
requirements.evidence: Keyhole hanger accessory on the base cell (accessory:0#0,0#0, slot 0) for hanging on wall screws.

Three hook plates (hex-acc-hook) with six hooks on slots 2-4 of the base cell. They are present, but the configurator only lets a cable coil, gaffer tape or FPV goggles hang on them, so no hand tools are shown on the hooks.

finish.summary: Built a single hex base cell as the rack body, with one keyhole hanger on its back face (slot 0) for hanging on screws already in a wall, three hook plates on the front faces (slots 2, 3, 4; two hooks each, six hooks total), and end caps on the two remaining open side faces. The check is clean (meshClash clear, no issues). The configurator does not allow hand tools (screwdriver, pliers, hex driver) to hang on the hook plates: the hook only takes a cable coil, gaffer tape or FPV goggles, and at this low height those would hang through the bench, so I did not dress the hooks. The rack is therefore a hook-and-keyhole rack ready for tools, but the tools themselves are not shown in the build. Material strength and wall-load ratings are not checked by the configurator.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
